title: Dujiangyan Irrigation System
aliases: Mount Qingcheng and the Dujiangyan Irrigation System
summary: Dujiangyan is a water-control system on the Minjiang River at the edge of the Chengdu plain in Sichuan, originally built around 256 BCE under Li Bing, a Qin official. UNESCO says it diverts water, drains sediment and controls floods and flow without dams, was enlarged under later dynasties, and now irrigates 668,700 hectares.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO says originally constructed around 256 BC (astronomical -255); Sixth Tone says completed in 251 BC (-250), so the start range allows 5 years later. End is the present: the system operates.

phases.description: UNESCO: originally constructed around 256 BC (the ICOMOS dossier says 256 BCE under Li Bing); Sixth Tone says completed in 251 BC.
The system was modified and enlarged under the Tang, Song, Yuan and Ming dynasties and still operates (UNESCO). Dates for the floodgate itself are not given.

importance.justification: UNESCO inscribed it in 2000 and describes it as an ecological engineering feat in use for over 2,250 years.

reviewer_note: The model is the Feishayan floodgate only (240 m long, 2 m high, ICOMOS dossier, which spells it Feiyashan), because the dossier gives dimensions for each component separately and mixing them would not describe one structure; shape wall with linear true. Point is the UNESCO property coordinate (N31 0 6.012 E103 36 19.008); the headworks are within about 1 km of it but this was not measured. The dossier gives the floodgate no date of its own, so phases follow the system (256 BCE per UNESCO, 251 BCE completion per Sixth Tone).
